items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: sometimes Butterbeans and Susie (unintelligible) would work the club.

ctx.x: she had a duo -- Martha Davis Davidson and spouse -- a beautiful pianist. And, Mr. Robinson's son, Mundy -- he was the same age I was -- he played drums and I played the fiddle. Mr. Robinson bought me a fiddle -- I think he paid $75 for it, and he said every week, I'd have to pay him so much until I paid for it myself.

Well, we worked this club -- we had a regular show -- 6 girls in the line; 2 tap dancers, sometimes Butterbeans and Susie (unintelligible) would work the club. It was kind of a popular little club -- they had a lot of popular little clubs in Chicago then.

But that's when I got my first, real bass violin. I was still going to school, high school, junior high, and Buster got a record date for me. I'll never forget this. And I had to get permission from my teacher to make it, although I'm working every night. We worked from, say, about 9 or 10 o' clock at night until the owner said, Mr. Robinson said, "You could go home now."
